title: Throughput Degradation Alerting, Circuit Orchestration, and Remediation Campaign
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigate repeated throughput shortfalls seen in dedicated pools over the last 3 incident windows and deliver a combined operational and code remediation plan. Focus areas: earlier detection of scaling regressions, fast graceful-degradation policies (circuit orchestration), and long-lived fixes to autoscaler heuristics. Deliverables: alert tuning, emergency circuit controller (software-level 'orchestrator' to gracefully trade latency for throughput), PRs for autoscaler hardening, and a documented postmortem + verification playbook.
updates: 2025-02-12 - Ticket created after recurring alerts showed 15-30% sustained throughput drop across multiple dedicated pools during peak - creator Aisha. Initial triage pointed at recent kernel selection rollout and autoscaler window changes.

2025-02-13 - Infra/Serving oncall (Marco) performed fast rollback of autoscaler window change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3219) which temporarily restored headroom; regression still reproducible in canary clusters.

2025-02-15 - Performed controlled repro in staging; confirmed change in kernel scheduling combined with request batching thresholds can amplify tail latency and cause autoscaler to undershoot. Experiment notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/staging-scaling-repro-2025-02-15.

2025-02-16 - Deployed temporary 'graceful-degrade' controller to canary pools: reduces max_batch_size and enables early-short-circuit for >95th percentile queue growth. Observed 12% throughput recovery under synthetic load.

2025-02-18 - Postmortem skeleton drafted (doc link below); preliminary decision to implement (1) autoscaler hysteresis and min-headroom leasing, (2) circuit orchestrator with per-customer knob, (3) kernel scheduler rollback and safer rollout gating.

2025-02-20 - Action owners assigned; added integration tests to avoid regression (see testing PR). Agreed to instrument additional signals (request queue length by campaign, batch-formation latency, per-GPU KV cache hit rate).

2025-02-25 - Began phased rollout of autoscaler hardening in non-critical pools; monitoring dashboards updated with new SLOs and an emergency alert threshold. Planning verification load test on 2025-03-03.
decisions: Implement a 'circuit orchestrator' running inside the serving plane that can apply graceful-degradation policies per pool: (a) degrade to lower-throughput knobs, (b) redirect to fallback model variants, (c) shed non-critical requests based on tagging.

Add autoscaler hysteresis and headroom leasing: autoscaler will maintain a rolling min-headroom percentage for 5 minutes before shrinking capacity and use a short-term emergency borrow policy for burst absorb.
Rollback kernel scheduler kernel-selection changes in the 2025-02-10 rollout while we add canary gating and microbenchmarks to validate batch-formation characteristics.
Introduce new alert: sustained queue-growth for 3 minutes at p99 batch formation latency > 120ms triggers P0 incident path for dedicated pools.
Require every autoscaler or scheduler change to include an end-to-end synthetic workload regression test in CI that simulates KV cache pressure and variable sequence lengths.
Add per-customer burst tags to telemetry so we can attribute noisy tenants and apply localized throttles instead of global capacity contraction.

notes: Root cause summary: interaction between a kernel-selection optimization (changed matrix for attention kernel selection) and a tightened autoscaler window produced a feedback loop: slower batch-formation increased queue signals which the autoscaler misinterpreted as demand falling, leading to underscale and further throughput loss.
This ticket focuses on both operational guardrails (alerts, headroom leasing, circuit orchestration) and long-term code fixes (safer kernel rollout, autoscaler logic).
We intentionally avoid global hard throttles; priority is localized controls (per-tenant tagging + per-pool soft-degrade) to reduce customer impact.
